findings.justification: Predates the range and sits on the stale-row path, not on refuseMissingSources: with core.symlinks=false git writes a committed link as a regular file holding its target path, so the path is present (not skipped) and the gate honestly scans what that checkout holds — the link's function is not there, so its row reads stale. Every gate that reads the working tree sees that checkout's content; judging the link's target instead would mean resolving 120000 blobs against HEAD's tree, a design change to what the ratchet reads. Stallion and its known vendor track no symlinks (git ls-files -s shows no 120000 entry), CI on the pushed tip (POSIX) refuses the red result, and the refusal the reviewer followed is the pre-existing stale-row fix.

findings.claim: (pass 4, over f8b9392..5a38d01) The rule that a skipped path HEAD holds nothing at 'has no source any commit keeps' is false under colocated jj: jj 0.44 writes every file ADDED in its working-copy commit into git's index as an intent-to-add entry (empty blob, status ' A'), and `jj commit` keeps that file even when jj's sparse patterns take it off disk. The gate read such a baselined source as stale rows, its printed --update-baseline stripped the ceiling, the local gate stayed green through `jj commit`, and the landed tip was red on a clean clone. Only a `git add -N` double pinned the rule; f8b9392's carry had kept this ceiling.
